record.title: European Commission opens expression of interest for cellular dual-use drone detection
record.summary: On 11 November 2026, the European Commission opened an expression of interest, closing 28 February 2027, to collect proposals and information on testing and deploying cellular-based dual-use drone detection. The consultation includes AI-based detection of connected drones, cellular sensing for non-connected drones, and integration with counter-drone response systems. EU Member States are invited to submit proposals with private-sector consortia, and Ukraine may participate. The Commission says it will consider a separate funding call after reviewing submissions; the current notice is not a funding award or deployment.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The European Commission opened an expression of interest on 11 November 2026, with a closing date of 28 February 2027, seeking proposals and information on cellular-based dual-use drone detection.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The Commission identifies AI-based detection of connected drones, cellular sensing for non-connected drones, and integration of detection/tracking with command-and-control and counter-drone systems as possible dimensions.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The Commission says it will explore whether to publish an official funding call for pilots after reviewing the expression-of-interest exercise; no funding call or award is established by this notice.

evidence_gaps.description: No project selection, funding call, award, deployed capability, technical specification or measured detection performance is reported.

brief.importance_rationale: If it leads to pilots, the initiative could shape EU counter-drone sensing and telecom integration for security and critical infrastructure. The present evidence is an information-gathering step, not a funding decision, deployment or performance result.
limitations: The consultation seeks proposals and information; it does not establish that a pilot will be funded.
AI-based detection is one of three possible dimensions, not a specified technical design or demonstrated capability.
No selected projects, deployment, operating results or detection performance are reported.

technical.claimed_result: The Commission’s expression of interest says its objective is to gather proposals on testing and deploying cellular-based dual-use drone detection, including AI-based detection of connected drones; it reports no performance result.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official page documents an expression of interest opened 11 November 2026 and closing 28 February 2027, the eligible proposal structure, and the possible—not committed—later funding call.
technical.mechanism: Potential work combines telecom-network sensing for connected drones, cellular sensing for non-connected drones, and integration with command-and-control and response systems. No concrete design is specified.
technical.regime: EU Member States and private-sector consortia; Ukraine may participate as part of a consortium. Information-gathering stage for dual-use counter-drone applications.
technical.reproducibility: This is a policy consultation announcement; the source text is directly inspectable. No technical system or operational result was evaluated.
technical.strongest_baseline: The Commission says the call follows the EU Action Plan on Drone and Counter Drone Security; no previous performance baseline is supplied.

brief.title: European Commission opens expression of interest for cellular dual-use drone detection
brief.why_it_matters: The exercise places AI-enabled telecom sensing and counter-drone integration on the EU security-policy agenda and could lead to cross-border pilots. It establishes an information-gathering step and possible future funding, not selected projects, deployed capability or measured detection performance.
